rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, there is no evidence to exploit, so the priority is establishing a clean reference point that maximizes the information value of subsequent ablations. config_003 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, no aggregation, concat) is the simplest multimodal configuration using the most common encoders (scgpt for RNA, ViT-L for image) and the simplest fusion (concat). It directly tests the study's primary hypothesis—whether combining RNA and image modalities improves validation accuracy—while keeping the design space minimal (single profile, no aggregation) so that any performance can be cleanly attributed. The natural follow-up experiment (config_004, rna_only singleprofile scgpt) would then isolate the image contribution with a single-variable comparison. Starting here gives the highest-leverage baseline from which to build a structured ablation ladder across profile setting, encoder choice, aggregation, and fusion strategy under the limited budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_003: multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, concat → acc 0.435), the single most important uncertainty is whether the image modality actually contributes meaningful signal or whether a simpler RNA-only model is competitive. config_004 (rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt, no aggregation, no fusion) is a clean single-variable ablation of config_003: the only difference is the removal of the image encoder and concat fusion, while keeping the same RNA encoder (scgpt), profile setting (singleprofile), and no aggregation. If config_004 matches or exceeds config_003, the image modality is not adding value and the search should pivot toward RNA-encoder and profile-setting choices. If config_003 is clearly better, multimodal fusion is justified and we can invest subsequent experiments in optimizing encoder choices, aggregation, and fusion strategy. This is the highest-information experiment under a tight budget because the answer reshapes the entire remaining search direction, and it changes exactly one design axis relative to the only data point we have.

Evidence: config_003 (multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, concat) achieved 0.4348 acc / 0.4234 F1, while config_004 (rna_only, scgpt, singleprofile) achieved 0.4106 acc / 0.3785 F1 — a ~2.4% accuracy and ~4.5% F1 gap. This is suggestive but based on a single pair, so it is unclear whether the image modality is a strong independent signal or whether the small gain is noise/complementarity. Question: config_025 (image_only, singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l) is the clean ablation that isolates the image modality's standalone contribution while holding the image encoder and profile setting identical to config_003. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It directly tests whether the 2.4% multimodal lift is driven by a genuinely informative image channel or by a weak/noisy addition. (2) The result will sharply guide all subsequent experiments — if image_only is weak, the multimodal benefit is complementary and we should prioritize fusion/aggregation design; if image_only is competitive, we should invest in stronger image encoders or multiprofile image aggregation. (3) It changes only the model setting (multimodal→image_only) relative to config_003, satisfying the principle of isolating one design variable. (4) Under a tight budget, resolving this fundamental question about modality value is more informative than, e.g., swapping fusion to weighted (config_031) or changing the image backbone (config_015), which are secondary refinements that depend on knowing whether the image signal is worth optimizing.

Evidence: config_003 (multimodal, scgpt+imagenet_vit_l, concat) achieves 0.4348 acc, only marginally above RNA-only config_004 (0.4106), while image-only config_025 is very weak (0.2266). This small multimodal gain raises the question of whether the image signal is genuinely useful but poorly integrated, or simply uninformative. Question: config_031 changes only the fusion strategy (concat → weighted) while holding all other settings identical to config_003 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, no aggregation). This isolates the effect of fusion on multimodal performance. Why this is the best next experiment: It is a single-variable comparison that directly tests whether a learned weighting can extract more value from the image modality. If weighted fusion improves over concat, it confirms the image carries useful signal and justifies further investment in multimodal configurations (aggregation, multiprofile, alternative encoders). If it does not, it strongly suggests the image modality with imagenet_vit_l is not contributing meaningfully, redirecting the remaining budget toward RNA encoder or profile-setting improvements. Under a limited budget, resolving this uncertainty about whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing is the highest-value information gain.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_003 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, concat) at 0.4348 acc, with RNA clearly dominant (rna_only 0.4106 vs image_only 0.2266) and concat slightly beating weighted fusion. The profile/aggregation axis is completely untested. Question: Does moving from singleprofile to multiprofile with simple avgpool aggregation improve performance while keeping the same encoders (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l) and the same fusion (concat)? Why this is the best next step: config_009 is the most direct, minimal extension of the current best config—only profile_setting and aggregation change, isolating the effect of multiprofile + aggregation. Using avgpool (rather than transformer) is a conservative first probe of this axis; if it helps, a follow-up with transformer aggregation becomes a clean comparison. This is more informative than jumping to a new encoder or a more complex aggregation, as it reduces uncertainty about whether the profile dimension matters at all before investing in more complex variants.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile + avgpool aggregation (config_009, acc=0.5176) substantially outperforms the singleprofile baseline (config_003, acc=0.4348), an ~8-point gain attributable to profile aggregation. The key open question is whether the aggregation method itself matters: does a learned transformer aggregation capture inter-profile interactions that a simple average pool misses, or is avgpool already near-optimal? config_001 changes only the aggregation (avgpool→transformer) relative to config_009, keeping scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, and concat fusion fixed, making it a clean single-variable test. This is preferred over testing fusion method (e.g., config_016) because aggregation is the more fundamental design axis in the multiprofile setting, and the expected performance delta is larger. A positive result would justify further investment in learned aggregation; a null or negative result would confirm that simple pooling suffices and redirect effort toward other axes (e.g., RNA encoder choice or image encoder). Under a tight budget, resolving this uncertainty about the most impactful multiprofile design choice is the highest-value next experiment.

Evidence: Multiprofile with avgpool+concat (config_009, acc=0.5176) substantially outperforms singleprofile multimodal (config_003, acc=0.4348), and in singleprofile the image-only model is very weak (0.2266) while RNA-only is moderate (0.4106). This suggests RNA is the dominant modality, but we have no multiprofile RNA-only baseline. Question: config_018 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) is the direct ablation of config_009 with the image modality removed, isolating how much of the multiprofile gain is driven by RNA profile aggregation versus the image contribution. Why best next: If RNA multiprofile alone approaches ~0.50, the image modality adds little and we should focus budget on RNA encoder/aggregation variants; if it drops substantially (e.g., <0.45), the image is essential in the multiprofile regime and we should prioritize image encoder and fusion choices. This single-variable ablation maximally reduces uncertainty about the most important architectural question before committing further experiments.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_018 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) at 0.5305 acc / 0.5152 F1, which surprisingly outperforms the best multimodal setup (config_009, 0.5176). This suggests the RNA representation is the dominant signal, yet we have only tested one RNA encoder (scgpt). Uncertainty: We have zero evidence on whether scvi_n200 or pca_n2000 would improve upon scgpt in the multiprofile setting. This experiment tests the RNA encoder choice in isolation (only rna_encoder changes from config_018), keeping the best-known profile setting (multiprofile) and aggregation (avgpool) fixed. If scvi_n200 exceeds scgpt, it reveals a better representation and opens a new search direction; if it underperforms, it confirms scgpt as the preferred encoder and lets us redirect budget toward fusion or image-encoder questions. Under a limited budget, resolving the RNA encoder question is more informative than re-testing aggregation (which already has moderate evidence favoring avgpool) because the RNA encoder is the primary signal in the top-performing model and remains completely unexplored.

The strongest evidence so far is that scvi_n200 dramatically outperforms scgpt as an RNA encoder (config_006: 0.650 acc vs config_018: 0.530 acc, both rna_only/multiprofile/avgpool). The critical open question is whether adding the image modality provides any benefit on top of this already-dominant RNA representation. For scgpt, multimodal did not help in the multiprofile setting (config_009: 0.518 < config_018: 0.530), but scvi_n200 is a fundamentally different learned latent and the interaction is unknown. config_029 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the minimal-change extension of config_006: it keeps the same RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation, and only adds the image branch with concat fusion (necessary for two modalities). This directly isolates the marginal contribution of image information given the best RNA encoder. If it matches or exceeds 0.650, image is additive; if it falls below, the scvi_n200 latent already captures what image would contribute, and future budget should focus on RNA-side improvements rather than multimodal fusion.

The current best is config_029 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat; acc 0.7150). The only untested dimension within this otherwise-optimal setting is aggregation method. With scgpt, avgpool (0.5176) narrowly beat transformer (0.5070), but scvi_n200 produces learned variational representations that may interact differently with attention-based aggregation. Config_014 changes only aggregation (avgpool→transformer) while holding encoder, image model, profile setting, and fusion constant, cleanly isolating this variable. If transformer helps, it opens a new optimization axis; if not, it confirms avgpool and redirects budget toward the image-encoder or fusion question. This is the highest-information single-variable test available for the current best configuration.
